newsitem.title: GERMANY: Profit-taking keeps German bond gain in check.
newsitem.headline: Profit-taking keeps German bond gain in check.

text.p: Profit-taking helped pull German debt off its session highs in late trading but failed to wipe out all gains amassed in Tuesday's unexpected surge higher, aided in part by weak German economic data.
By 1553 GMT the December Bund future contract traded on Frankfurt's DTB exchange was up 26 basis points at 102.69, having charged as high as 102.99.

Dealers said profit-taking was the natural response to the day's unexpected move higher, which many dealers were at a loss to explain. The Bundesbank's insistence rates will remain steady in the near-term also helped curb gains.

The Bundesbank restated it sees no reason for interest rates to be changed in the near-term, leaving economists confident of their predictions that all three key German rates will remain steady at Thursday's bi-weekly council meeting.
The market shot higher in early trading, boosted by a 1.8 percent decline in German October industrial output on the month.

"The numbers were very helpful," said Ros Lifton, senior international economist at HSBC Markets in London. But she added fundamentals were no longer driving the market which was infected by strong optimism flooding the U.S. market.
After the strong climb, some dealers said the market may try to catch its breath before a slew of U.S. economic data, expected in the later part of the week.
But generally dealers were unsure what the market's next move would be, saying after the day's slightly irrational performance, the market could head anywhere in the next sessions.
At the same time dealers do not see a massive sell-off, saying the 102.30 line was an intermediary support level.
